notes: Creativity 2 rests on one small art-therapy sponsorship; 1 is defensible if art therapy is not treated as arts sponsorship. Community: customer education is commercially motivated (effectiveness is partly measured by 'sales outcomes from participants'), which edges toward the 'educating customers as marketing' trap. It was still counted as external education because it is substantive clinical training with nonprofit and academic partners and an LMIC target. Level 4 is arguable ('Investing in education continues to be part of our core business'); the lower level was chosen because I was torn. Contradiction: the CEO letter says education was 'intensified', but the metrics show activities fell from 12 000 to 10 700 and participants from 400 000 to 370 000 versus 2024. Past programs, recorded as context only: Stiftung Schönes Lächeln (Switzerland), It's for Kids (Germany), Present a tree (Russia) and Krebsliga Pink Team (Switzerland), all marked Completed. Women in leadership rose to 39.4% against a 45% 2030 target; this is a demographic outcome and was not separately scored. The 'learn and grow' employee score target is 'Not on track' (76 versus a target of 80). Affected communities (S3) was assessed as non-material in the double materiality assessment.
